note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses), round 1. The 15-17 Oct round left no record for this task, so this review was run on 18 Oct on the new device. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: The item is sound in most respects, but one medium finding survives: the first requirement (bit rate 4 kbit/s) is never checked independently of the demodulator gain. One low finding covers the trace sign. Everything else I tested held up. (1) Solvable from the instruction and the start graph alone: samples_per_symbol = 48000/4000 = 12, a Gaussian BT of about 0.3 (the standard GSM value; Murota-Hirade tables give a 99.9 % bandwidth of 1.33 Rb at BT 0.5 > 1.25 Rb, so BT 0.5 must go), and a Quadrature Demod gain of samp_rate/(2*pi*1000). All three can go in one atomic change_graph edit. (2) The instruction states every number the oracle uses (skip 4096, 4 kbit/s, +-1 kHz, 99.9 % within +-2.5 kHz, 1.0 within 3 %, RMS 1.0 within 5 %, mean 0 within +-0.1 kHz). It names both File Sinks with their item types, and it leaks no parameter values. The 71,680-item run needs no statement: the Random Source repeats by default, and even with repeat off it gives 9.6 M samples. (3) Family and level are right: parameter-tune, L2, 7 functional blocks with modulation (GMSK Mod interpolates) and demodulation. The reference differs from the start only in parameter values. (4) Valid alternatives pass ./gb ladder: BT 0.40 (band 0.999188), 0.20 (0.999882), 0.15 (0.999939), 0.10 (0.999929), and a literal gain of 7.64 (peak 1.000078). The three variants also pass. BT 0.45 is correctly rejected (0.998864 < 0.999, consistent with theory). (5) A channel low-pass filter used instead of a smaller BT is rejected because the trace peak rises to 1.22 / 1.31 (> 1.03). That is the stated trace rule, so rejecting it is correct. (6) The authoring note says the HW Impairments frequency offset does not move the signal. Confirmed: with freq_offset = 0.1 the output stays within 1e-5 of the reference. Scratch work: WSL ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-19/ (gbf19_alts.py, gbf19_corr.py, alts/*.grc, *.result.json, *_obs/).

findings.claim: The bit rate, the first stated requirement, is checked only through max|trace| = gain x (bit_rate/4). Any wrong bit rate passes when the Quadrature Demod gain is re-fitted to it. The gain that does this is GNU Radio's own idiom: digital.gmsk_demod sets quadrature_demod_cf(1/sensitivity), i.e. gain = 2*sps/pi. Written in terms of samples_per_symbol, that normalises the peak to 1.0 for every samples_per_symbol, so the f2p check no longer depends on the bit rate at all. For the correct sps 12 this idiom is a valid answer (2*12/pi = 7.639 = 48000/(2*pi*1000)). With a wrong sps it is a wrong answer that passes. The authoring notes record only the special case of a consistent sample-rate change.
findings.evidence: Every graph below was run through ./gb ladder (ladder.check) with the task's task.json, and every one reached V6 with all four checks passing, although its bit rate is wrong. w08_sps16_gain_inv_sensitivity.grc (variable sps = 16, samples_per_symbol: sps, gain: 2*sps/math.pi; 3 kbit/s) gave first_failed None: peak 1.000005, band 0.999928, rms 0.999998, mean -0.0205. w01 (sps 16, gain samp_rate/(2*math.pi*750)) gave the same values. w02 (sps 10, BT 0.2, gain samp_rate/(2*math.pi*1200); 4.8 kbit/s) gave band 0.999441. w09 (sps 11, 4.36 kbit/s) gave band 0.999179, and w10 (sps 13, 3.69 kbit/s) gave band 0.999812. w05 (samp_rate 96000, sps 24, gain formula unchanged; read at 48 kHz this is 2 kbit/s with +-0.5 kHz) gave peak 1.000007 and band 0.99994. Only 6 kbit/s is caught, by the bandwidth check (w03/w04: 0.99759 / 0.99878). The idiom is at /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/gnuradio/digital/gmsk.py:224-225. The mutation set contains only single-parameter edits, so no mutant covers this pattern. A fix that works was calibrated with gbf19_corr.py: corr_ref of freq_trace.dat against the reference trace is gain- and sign-invariant (normalised |vdot|), and the random bytes are deterministic in the harness (analog_random_source_x calls numpy.random.randint at construction, after the worker's np.random.seed(0)). Settings: x = trace[4096 : 4096+5376], ref = reference trace[4352 : 4352+5120], max_lag 1024, which gives 4,096 correlated samples and covers relative delays from -256 to +768. Valid answers score 1.0 (reference, v2, literal gain), 0.9978 (v3, BT 0.35), 0.9961 (v1, BT 0.25), 0.9931 (BT 0.40), 0.9878 (BT 0.45), 0.9789 (BT 0.20), 0.9376 (BT 0.15) and 0.8677 (BT 0.10). The channel-filter graphs x02 / x03, rejected anyway by the peak rule, score 0.99. Wrong bit rates score 0.13-0.25 (w01/w08 0.136, w02 0.152, w05 0.160, w09 0.136, w10 0.243, w03 0.242, w04 0.249).
findings.suggested_fix: Add an f2p check {point: trace, feature: corr_ref, ref: <reference trace samples 4352..9471 (5,120 values)>, skip: 4096, n: 5376, max_lag: 1024, min: 0.5, property: bit_rate}. Generate ref in build.py from a kept reference run (gbf-test-17 already stores an inline corr_ref reference of 4,352 samples). Starting the reference 256 samples late lets the lag search cover answers with less delay than the reference. A max_lag of 1024 covers a long added filter: with max_lag 512 the Blackman LPF graph x03 scored only 0.365, because its ~440-sample delay fell outside the window. In the check's note, record that it relies on the stated 'keep the random byte source' and on the harness seeding numpy with 0. Add the mutants sps -> 16 with gain 2*sps/math.pi, sps 10 + BT 0.2 + gain samp_rate/(2*math.pi*1200), and samp_rate 96000 + sps 24 (each breaks bit_rate). Update spec_properties.bit_rate.checked_by and re-run the gates.

findings.claim: The trace sign is not checked. The instruction requires that freq_trace.dat 'shows the instantaneous frequency in kHz', but a negated trace (negative gain, upper and lower frequencies swapped) passes every check. The proposed corr_ref fix (F1) does not catch it either, because corr_ref takes |vdot|. The limit is recorded only in authoring_notes.oracle_limits.
findings.evidence: w07_negative_gain.grc (reference with gain -samp_rate/(2*math.pi*1000)) gave first_failed None: peak 1.000004, band 0.999667, rms 0.999997, mean +0.0239 (reference -0.0239). Its trace is exactly the negated reference trace (max|w07 + ref| = 0), and its corr_ref against the reference is 1.0.
findings.suggested_fix: Either give oracles.corr_ref an opt-in 'signed' flag (use the real part of vdot without abs, so a negated trace scores -1) and set it on the F1 check, which rejects an inverted trace and still accepts every listed valid answer; or keep the limit and copy it into review.notes so the team accepts it explicitly (authoring_notes do not appear on the team review sheet).

compliance.verdict: The item passes every mechanical compliance check. Two low findings remain: some stated 'keep' requirements are not observable and have no graph check, and the oracle limits are not surfaced for the team review. Gates: I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates on a scratch copy (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-19/task); the task directory itself was not touched. The resulting gates.json equals the stored one: solvability 10/10 with 8 workers, 610 tokens, 3/3 variants reach V6, start fails at V6 with only f2p failing, and 16/16 mutants reach V5 with a kill rate of 1.0. Split: the seed channels/demo_gmsk.grc is 'test' in splits/flowgraph_seed_split.json. Its SHA-256 768ba6ab... matches both the installed example and task.json, and it is on the training team's 'do not use' list. Licence (GPL-3.0-or-later, derived from the GNU Radio example), source, derivation (checked against the original file), cluster_id, provenance, and review (pending-team-review) are all correct. The perturbation record matches build.py. Every mutant is spec-breaking (the BT 0.5 mutant leaves 0.99852 < 0.999; gain x1.1 is outside 3 %). Tolerances are the stated ones. build.py run twice in a scratch mirror gave task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and all variants byte-identical to the task's. The schema validates, and the canary appears only in task.json. id, directory and split agree. Disjointness: no training spec uses demo_gmsk. t21_gmsk_pipe_build (build) and t10_param_tuning (centre frequency / bandwidth retune) are named and are different tasks. Near-duplicates: none in items/tier_f/*/*. gbf-test-14 (NBFM loopback build) also tests the Quadrature Demod gain formula fs/(2*pi*deviation), but its family, modulation and structure differ; this is a note for the set critic.

findings.claim: Two of the instruction's 'Keep everything else as it is' requirements have no observable effect and no graph check: 'the 48 kHz sample rate' and 'the HW Impairments block'. A graph that breaks either one passes. The mutation set suggests otherwise. The mutant samp_rate -> 32000 (breaks: sample_rate) is killed only because the reference writes the gain as samp_rate/(2*math.pi*1000); its gmsk_iq.dat is identical to the reference's. spec_properties.sample_rate ('checked indirectly: every frequency check assumes 48 kHz') is therefore not accurate.
findings.evidence: w06_samp32k_literal_gain.grc (samp_rate 32000, gain 7.639437268410976, sps 12, BT 0.3) passes V6. Both of its output files are bit-identical to the reference's (max|diff| = 0 for iq and for trace). w11_impairments_bypassed.grc (channels_impairments_0 removed with edit.bypass) passes V6, with outputs within 4e-6 of the reference. I evaluated two p2p graph checks with graph_checks.evaluate: block_present {ids: [channels_impairments]} and block_present {ids: [variable], params: {value: '48000'}}. Both pass on the reference, the start and all three variants, and on BT alternatives such as a02. The first rejects w11; the second rejects w06 and w05 (samp_rate 96000).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the two p2p graph checks above, with properties channel_unchanged / sample_rate, and update spec_properties.sample_rate.checked_by. Alternatively, reword the keep-list behaviourally and drop the structural wording. Optionally add the mutants 'bypass channels_impairments_0' and 'samp_rate 32000 with a literal gain' so the mutation gate exercises these properties directly. Re-run the gates.

findings.claim: The item's known oracle gaps appear only in task.json authoring_notes.oracle_limits: the trace sign, and a consistent sample-rate change with rescaled sps and gain. review.notes is empty, and ./gb tier-f sheet shows neither authoring_notes nor spec_properties. The team therefore reviews this item without seeing which stated requirements the oracle cannot check, although the 16 Oct oracle policy requires every stated requirement to be checked.
findings.evidence: In task.json, review.notes is '' and authoring_notes.oracle_limits reads 'trace sign not observable (zero-mean data); a consistent sample-rate change plus rescaled sps/gain is not detected (the instruction forbids it)'. src/grcbench/tier_f/cli.py 'sheet' writes only the instruction, the observation contract, the oracle check summaries and the gate status. Item-quality F1 shows that the second limit is wider than recorded: any samples_per_symbol passes with gain = 2*sps/pi.
findings.suggested_fix: After the item-quality F1/F2 fixes, write the limits that remain into review.notes (or into the sheet), so the team decides on them explicitly. If the corr_ref and graph-check fixes are adopted, remove the stale oracle_limits text.
